title: Starting a New Season
excerpt: How is it October already?
content:
I am late! How did it get to be October before my first Substack post! Well… excuses of course, but I picked up a new prep at school and it is overwhelming. Don’t let the lack of a post from me let you think I haven’t been busy, because OH I HAVE!

1. This summer I signed a 6-month YouTube partnership with RallyOrder. Alex and Riley have been super to work with, but I have never managed a partnership contract before. I plan to overdeliver for them, which will have benefits for you too. All my upcoming YouTube videos will be add-free, except for a 60-second midroll about RallyOrder. I’m going to drop the midroll here, and if you have a school store but haven’t checked out RallyOrder, you really should. The link below looks like my most recent video, but it cuts straight to the RallyOrder midroll.

2. I launched my first ever website- www.thebowtiegoat.com. I’m using Claude to build it, and the process has really been so much fun. I know my support for the DECA community has been unorganized. I knew a website could really pull it all together. In fact, I’ve sat on the domain for more than a year without the time to make it all come together. Finally… FINALLY it has. I’m pretty proud of the work so far. I am especially proud of the event preparation materials. Let me highlight them:

  • EVENT SELECTION: I haven’t loved how hard it is to help students pick events. This page makes it easier (in my mind at least).

  • ROLE PLAYS: Across the past few years as BowtieGOAT, I have written numerous role plays. I have always intended to offer my previous year’s role plays online for free, like DECA does. I am also frustrated that DECA has not updated all their free role plays to the new rubric format. So as I post mine, I also update them. It was a fun 3-hour challenge to get my Individual Series role plays posted. Then I tackled the Principles ones. I have PFL and TDM events remaining. Total I have 65 role plays uploaded with more to come.

  • ROLE PLAY MASTERY: Once we get students in events, it’s sort of hard to explain role plays to them. I organized some of my best videos for this process all in one spot. Rather than linking to all my videos separately, you can see them all here. Yes, I am going to remake these for the new rubric too. I’m aiming for mid-late October for that timeline.

  • I also coded a game into the site. It’s an Easter egg to find. But, you all can click the link here to find it! Enjoy!

3. But wait… Announcing the soft launch, version 1.0 of BowtieGOAT Prep. While my main page will remain free, this site will only be accessible to paying chapters.

Have you ever struggled to design a prep strategy for students across 60 different competitive events to help them all get to the DECA stage? Or, to simply keep track of them all? So have I. I am building the prep site to align all those issues.

Your students will log into the site and choose their event. The advisor will set the date of your competitions. Then the site backmaps prep from the current date to competition date. It will provide weekly work for your students without any input from you. The advisor will get a dashboard of your students and a simple stoplight feature to see who is on track.

This year’s version 1.0 will only be available to annually paid Substack subscribers. I want to test the site with a small cohort of advisors and students before a full launch next year. I am sure some it will break, but I am also sure it will provide value to your chapters this year.

I will detail more about this offering in next week’s Substack post.

4. Oh, I’m helping run a local chapter too. And have five kids. And… life.

I am committed to this community of advisors- those of us who are committed to our students but also likely do not have the time to do everything we want. My goal this year remains as it always has been. Do whatever I can to make your work a bit easier each year.

Thanks everyone!

Oh, Substack now has an AI filter. Trust me, I write all these in a Google Doc- but lacking an editor and in my impatience to post Substacks frequently, I do use Gemini to help make my thoughts more… thoughtful. If you want to see that original draft to compare, feel free!
